title: Release Contract and Local Gate Baseline
concrete_capability_transition: Brownie gains an executable fail-closed Release Engineering Contract and repository-local Release Gate plan that binds Rust, Node, Brownie guard, and recovery evidence to one audited source-of-truth before any Release Ready claim.

strategic_capability_mapping.transition: Release evidence is now modeled as an executable contract with required conditions, commit trace fields, artifact evidence slots, owner-controlled blockers, and a finite A-through-G plan.
strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: This does not claim product completion; it removes ambiguity from the remaining runtime-release-guard-ci blocker and prevents Release Ready from becoming a prose-only decision.

answers.strategic_capabilities: The phase advances headless_autonomous_development by making Release Ready mechanically auditable from one Runtime-owned release contract and local gate plan.
answers.new_capability: A contributor can run pnpm release:gate -- --dry-run to inspect the exact mandatory command plan and run guard:release-contract to fail closed when required release conditions, trace fields, artifact evidence, or workflow-scope blockers are missing.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: The prior audit named runtime-release-guard-ci but did not define one contract tying required-before-release closure, Product Completion Guard, CI, artifacts, SBOM, checksum, provenance, reviews, and owner settings to a single fail-closed decision.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie could continue merging release-readiness changes while treating missing workflow hardening, artifacts, SBOM, checksums, signatures, provenance, and independent reviews as informal follow-up rather than release-blocking evidence.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase does not reopen closed ledger, platform, deadline, durability, or protocol work; it defines the Release Engineering Contract that composes those already guarded results with future artifact and governance gates.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. No JSON-RPC method or Runtime protocol surface is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The new release contract is a guard-owned source-of-truth artifact, not a user-facing summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Release guard behavior changes: incomplete artifact, trace, owner-setting, workflow-scope, or review evidence now keeps runtime_release_ready false through an executable guard.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Autonomous release phases now have a bounded command plan and machine-readable stop conditions instead of relying on controller prose or external state as authority.
answers.milestone_progress: RRP-8.2 converts the final runtime-release-guard-ci blocker from a vague CI hardening item into a finite Release Contract with local gate evidence and explicit external blockers.

non_goals: scheduler, durable queue, supervisor, SaaS, RBAC, Vault, BDK, or Enterprise admin

reject_when: phase claims Runtime Release Ready or raises maturity without generated release evidence
missing artifacts, missing SBOM, missing checksum, missing signature or integrity proof, missing provenance, missing tested_commit, or missing workflow_run_id are treated as success
Release Ready conditions are split across unguarded prose instead of docs/architecture/runtime-release-contract.json
pnpm release:gate omits required Rust, Node, Brownie guard, or recovery commands
guard:release-contract is absent from the existing CI-invoked VSIX check path
workflow files are modified without workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent path
self-review is counted as independent human review
license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or signing infrastructure are changed by Runtime automation

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-8.2 changes release and phase guard engines. Review must confirm the Release Contract is fail-closed, local release:gate enumerates mandatory evidence without claiming success, VSIX check invokes the release contract guard and test, GitHub workflow hardening remains blocked_external without workflow scope, and runtime_release_ready stays false.

exit_criteria: docs/architecture/runtime-release-contract.json defines fail-closed Release Ready conditions, commit trace fields, artifact evidence slots, owner actions, external blockers, and the finite Phase A through G campaign.
scripts/release-gate.mjs exposes pnpm release:gate and a dry-run command plan for mandatory Rust, Node, Brownie guard, and recovery evidence.

scripts/guard-release-contract.mjs and its node:test suite fail closed for missing conditions, fake artifact success, missing package scripts, missing VSIX check integration, and missing workflow-scope blocker.
scripts/guard-runtime-release-readiness.mjs requires the release engineering contract reference and keeps runtime_release_ready false while it is partial.
extensions/brownie-vsix/package.json invokes guard:release-contract and guard:release-contract:test through the existing CI-invoked check path.
runtime_release_ready remains false and direct .github workflow hardening remains blocked_external until workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent CI hardening exists.
behavior_evidence: pnpm release:gate -- --evidence /tmp/brownie-rrp8-2-release-gate.json fails closed at rust_clippy after fmt and check pass because existing Runtime clippy warnings remain.

accepted_capability: Release Ready now has a Runtime-owned contract artifact with explicit required evidence and fail-closed missing-evidence semantics.
The repository-local release gate plan can be inspected and run from the same commit without requiring workflow-file mutation.
The existing CI-invoked VSIX check path now exercises the release contract guard and its failure-mode tests.
behavior_evidence: guard-release-contract tests reject missing release conditions, premature runtime_release_ready, fake artifact evidence, missing package scripts, missing VSIX integration, and missing workflow-scope blocker.
guard-runtime-release-readiness tests require the release contract audit reference and continue to reject stale not-ready or premature ready states.
release-gate dry-run records the exact command sequence for Rust, Node, Brownie guard, and real process-loss recovery evidence.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains execution, admission, replay, permission, MCP, workspace mutation, durable state, protocol, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
GitHub workflow settings, branch protection, protected tags, signing authority, license choice, and publish posture remain owner-controlled until explicitly provided.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as release evidence.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not edit .github workflow files without workflow scope.
Does not generate or publish release artifacts, tags, packages, license metadata, signatures, or release assets.

Does not add hosted scheduler, daemon, durable queue, supervisor, SaaS control plane, customer RBAC, Vault, billing, BDK, Enterprise admin, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or remote Git capability expansion.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected marking runtime-release-guard-ci closed because mandatory workflow wiring, artifacts, security scans, SBOM, checksum, provenance, and owner-controlled settings are not yet complete.
Rejected a documentation-only Release Ready definition because missing evidence must be executable guard failure.
Rejected editing .github/workflows/ci.yml because the active credentials do not have workflow scope.
technical_debt: runtime-release-guard-ci remains open until repo-local release scripts, permitted CI paths, workflow hardening, clippy -D warnings, artifacts, security scans, cross-platform smoke tests, soak evidence, and governance settings are complete.
Owner license, publish posture, signing or integrity mechanism, branch protection, protected tags, and independent reviews remain required before Runtime Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Proceed to supply-chain and artifact evidence phases that can be implemented in repository-local scripts without workflow scope, then return to direct CI wiring when workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent path exists.

runtime_release_dod: Closed RRP-1 through RRP-7.2 and RRP-5.18 evidence remains in force and is not reimplemented.
RRP-8.2 establishes the Release Engineering Contract and local gate baseline while keeping runtime_release_ready false.
Missing release artifacts, scans, SBOM, checksums, signatures or integrity proof, provenance, workflow run, tested commit, and independent reviews remain release-blocking.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, durable queues, worker leases, hosted isolation, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside local Runtime v0.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside this phase.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging publication, license choice, signing authority, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain owner-controlled or later release work.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-8.2.

technical_debt.next_action: Implement remaining repository-local supply-chain, artifact, provenance, cross-platform, soak, and governance gates, then wire mandatory workflow once workflow scope or an owner-approved equivalent path exists.
Owner must provide workflow-scope credentials or approve an equivalent CI-hardening path before direct .github workflow gate closure.
Owner must choose license and publish posture before public OSS release.

closeout_review.evidence: RRP-8.2 defines the release engineering contract and local gate baseline but does not claim artifact, security, cross-platform, governance, workflow, or owner-setting completion.
